_provenance.method: each compiled Noir artifact embeds its own main.nr in file_map; the 14 generic arguments are read verbatim from it
_provenance.validation: every tuple is cross-checked against the artifact's OWN abi - dg1/dg15/ec/sa/pk array lengths must equal DG1_LEN/DG15_LEN/EC_LEN/SA_LEN/N - and against the //name comment, which rarimo's generator derives from the same parameters. 25 of 75 artifacts failed that check (22 declare dg1 as [u8; 0], which no passport profile can be); 24 were rescued from a '-fix' re-release of the same profile, which is what those tags exist for.
_provenance.coverage: 75 of the 76 committed verifiers. ID_Card_I is the exception and cannot be regenerated: its VK matches no published asset, including the TD1 profile it was diffed against. rarimo additionally publishes 6 registerIdentity profiles this repo does not have, four of them TD1 - see TODO task 24.

10_256_3_3_576_248_1_1184_5_264.note: The artifact's own //name comment reads ..._0_1184_5_264 while the asset is named ..._1_1184_5_264 - AA_SIG_TYPE is 0 in the circuit, 1 in the name. RESOLVED as an upstream naming bug rather than a parameter ambiguity: our committed verifier shares all 61 VK constants with rarimo's published .sol of this name, and NO asset exists under the _0_ name, so this circuit is the one this file was built from. AA_SIG_TYPE=0 is legal - not_passports_zk_circuits.nr:625 guards `if (AA_SIG_TYPE != 0)`, i.e. carry DG15 without verifying its key.

14_256_1_4_1752_576_1_1496_3_512.provenance: TD1. RECOVERED. Two separate defects, both ours rather than upstream. (1) The generics were mis-decoded - DG1_LEN was 0 (TD1 is 95) and EC_LEN held a shift value - and were re-derived from the circom builder parameter list. (2) extract_dg15_pk_hash hardcoded a 128-byte read, assuming every RSA AA key is 1024-bit; this one is 768-bit.
14_256_1_4_1752_576_1_1496_3_512.provenance_aa_key: AA_SHIFT(64) + modulus(96) + exponent(5) = 165 = DG15_LEN exactly, zero slack, so the AA key is 768-bit. The 128-byte read ran 27 bytes past the end of dg15, which is why it looked unbuildable. I had also argued no DER layout puts a modulus at offset 64 - refuted by our own data: every working ECDSA-AA profile sits far past its bare-SPKI offset (251 vs ~27, 349 vs ~26), so a dg15 prefix is normal.
14_256_1_4_1752_576_1_1496_3_512.why_no_new_generic: The reader now selects on whether a 1024-bit key physically fits (AA_SHIFT + 128 > DG15_LEN), which is an exact structural test rather than a tuned threshold, and needs no 15th generic. A "largest standard modulus that fits" rule was rejected instead: it would pick 192- or 256-byte keys for four groups of profiles that work today with 1024-bit keys. All 40 existing RSA-AA profiles have AA_SHIFT=32 with DG15_LEN >= 163, so 160 fits and their chunking - and hash - is unchanged.

14_256_3_4_336_64_1_1480_5_296.derived: DERIVED 2026-08-10 (sec. 2.18gv). signals=6834. ⚠️ C(N=26,AA)=1502 is INTERPOLATED, not measured - no N=26 profile exists in both repos. Justified by C being near-flat in N for AA profiles (1498 at N=18, 1506 at N=35, slope 0.47/limb), but it is the only value here not directly calibrated. DG1_SHIFT=8 is also outside the 23..33 band. THE LEAST TRUSTWORTHY OF THE SIX.

1_160_3_4_576_200_NA.derived: DERIVED 2026-08-10, NOT read from a Noir artifact - rarimo publishes none for this profile. Method in TODO sec. 2.18gv: rarimo's CIRCOM release ships a ~2.8 MB -mobile.zip containing circom's generated C++, which declares get_main_input_signal_no(). That is an equation, signals = 8*(DG1_LEN + DG15_LEN + EC_LEN + SA_LEN) + C, with C calibrated per input-shape class from profiles present in BOTH repos. Here signals=4242 and C(N=18,no-AA)=1098 from 11_256_3_2_336_216_NA, giving EC_LEN=208. DG1_SHIFT and EC_SHIFT come from the name (fields 5 and 6 over 8, verified 78/78); SA_LEN from the EC_SHIFT + HASH_ALGO == SA_LEN identity (76/78). ⚠️ UNVALIDATED SEMANTICALLY: it satisfies every bounds check, but a wrong offset compiles cleanly and would verify the wrong bytes.

1_256_1_5_2376_336_1_2120_4_512.provenance: TD1. RECOVERED from quarantine - it was never corrupt, it was mis-decoded. DG1_LEN had been 0 (TD1 is 95) and EC_LEN had been overwritten with a shift value, producing the bogus "DG1_SHIFT == EC_LEN" signature it was quarantined for. Re-derived via rarimo circom RegisterIdentityBuilder, whose 10 template parameters are the profile name in order; that decoding was validated first (NA form 8/8 at 38/38, 10-field form 8/9 at 44/44). EC_LEN=297 = DG15_SHIFT + DG_HASH_ALGO, the dg15-hash-last pattern holding 41/44, and inside the SHA-256 padding cap of 311. DG15_LEN=229 was already recorded and falls inside the [192,247] window forced by the AA read below and padding above.
1_256_1_5_2376_336_1_2120_4_512.caveat: Compiling proves the tuple is SELF-CONSISTENT, not that it matches real documents of this class. DG15_LEN is the one field pinned only to a range [192,247] rather than derived; 229 is the recorded value and is used as-is. If proofs fail against a real TD1 of this class, DG15_LEN is the field to revisit first.

1_256_3_6_336_560_1_2744_4_256.derived: DERIVED 2026-08-10 (sec. 2.18gv). signals=7314, C(N=18,AA)=1498. ⚠️ DG1_SHIFT=70 is outside the 23..33 band - same caveat as 20_256_3_5_336_72_NA, though less extreme relative to its EC_LEN. UNVALIDATED SEMANTICALLY.

20_160_3_3_736_200_NA.derived: DERIVED 2026-08-10 (sec. 2.18gv). signals=4690, C(N=6,no-AA)=2122 calibrated from 20_256_3_3_336_224_NA. ⚠️ UNVALIDATED SEMANTICALLY.

20_256_3_5_336_248_25_2120_5_1816.provenance: RECOVERED. AA_SIG_TYPE 25 is brainpoolP384r1 (48-byte coordinates), confirmed by reading verify_signature branch 25, which builds BrainpoolP384r1Fr. extract_dg15_pk_hash had no branch for it and fell through to 32 bytes, reading both coordinates from the wrong offsets; the branch is now implemented.
20_256_3_5_336_248_25_2120_5_1816.provenance_dg15_len: DG15_LEN=323 = AA_SHIFT(227) + 2*48, the point being 04 || X(48) || Y(48) ending the structure. That identity holds EXACTLY on 6 of the 7 ECDSA-AA profiles (the exception, 28_384..., carries 40 trailing bytes). The recorded 283 satisfied neither the correct 48-byte read (needs 323) nor even the incorrect 32-byte one (needs 291), so it was wrong under any reading.
20_256_3_5_336_248_25_2120_5_1816.name_field_dg15_block_number_is_wrong: The name encodes DG15_BLOCK_NUMBER=5, which caps dg15 at 5*64-9 = 311 and so contradicts DG15_LEN=323. That cap formula is not in doubt - a control shows 44 of 45 profiles sit within 64 bytes of their cap, five of them at 298 against 311, which is only possible with 64-byte blocks. So the name field is the wrong one, and it is THE ONLY FIELD THE NOIR CIRCUIT NEVER USES: the generics take DG15_LEN in bytes, and BLOCK_NUMBER exists only in the circom naming. Taking AA_SHIFT and the curve as authoritative - both independently corroborated - and correcting the block count to 6 costs nothing in the circuit and is recorded here rather than silently ignored.
20_256_3_5_336_248_25_2120_5_1816.fails_closed: If DG15_LEN is nonetheless wrong, the dg15 hash will not match the value committed in ec and the circuit rejects genuine documents. It cannot accept forged ones - the failure direction is safe.

20_256_3_5_336_72_NA.derived: DERIVED 2026-08-10 (sec. 2.18gv). signals=5714, C(N=6,no-AA)=2122. ⚠️⚠️ THE WEAKEST OF THE SIX: DG1_SHIFT=9 lies OUTSIDE the 23..33 band that all 78 known profiles occupy. The name says 72/8=9 and that mapping is 78/78 exact elsewhere, so it is either a genuinely unusual layout or a sign this profile does not follow the convention. Do not deploy without an independent check.

20_256_3_6_336_248_NA.from: rarimo release artifact (recovered 2026-08-04, TODO sec. 2.18cz) - these 7 were published across earlier releases and were missing from the original recovery, which read only one release. Generics read verbatim from the artifact-embedded main.nr and cross-checked against that artifact's OWN abi (dg1/ec/sa/pk lengths all agree).

21_160_1_2_560_576_NA.provenance: TD1. RECOVERED. Generics re-derived from the circom builder parameter list (DG1_LEN=95 for TD1, DG1_SHIFT=72, EC_SHIFT=70, SA_LEN=90); the old ones were mis-decoded, with DG1_LEN=0 and EC_LEN holding a shift value.
21_160_1_2_560_576_NA.provenance_ec_len: EC_LEN=119 is FORCED, with no free parameter. An LDSSecurityObject entry is SEQUENCE{INTEGER dg, OCTET STRING hash} = 7 + hash bytes, so EC_LEN = DG1_SHIFT + hash + n*(7+hash) [+16 for ldsVersionInfo]. That model fits 69/85 exactly and the remaining 16-byte cluster is the optional ldsVersionInfo. Here hash=20 and DG1_SHIFT=72, giving 92 + 27n [+16]. Three candidates fall in the available window [92,119], and two are eliminated: n=0 (EC_LEN 92, and 108 with ldsVersionInfo) would mean DG1 is the LAST data group, which happens in 0 of 85 profiles - no document omits the face image - while n=2 gives 146, past the SHA-1 padding cap of 2*64-9 = 119. Only n=1 survives, and 119+9 = 128 fills exactly two blocks, which is why EC_BLOCK_NUMBER is 2.
21_160_1_2_560_576_NA.caveat: EC_LEN is the one field derived structurally rather than read from an artifact. If it is wrong the circuit FAILS CLOSED - it would reject genuine documents of this class, not accept forged ones - so the risk is a dead profile, never a false accept. Revisit EC_LEN first if a real TD1 of this class fails to register.

28_384_3_3_576_264_24_2024_4_2792.provenance: RECOVERED from quarantine by implementing the missing verify_signature branch, not by relaxing anything. SIG_TYPE 28 is secp384r1 (NIST P-384) with SHA-384. It had no branch, and because verify_signature returns nothing and asserts internally, that meant the document signature was NEVER CHECKED for this profile - a soundness hole, not a missing feature. verify_secp384r1_ecdsa was already vendored in sigver/ecdsa.nr and simply unreferenced.
28_384_3_3_576_264_24_2024_4_2792.curve_identification: N=8, EC_FIELD_SIZE=384, SHA-384 - the same shape as SIG_TYPE 25 (brainpoolP384r1). Of the two 384-bit curves in ICAO use brainpool is already 25, and secp384r1 is the only curve missing from an otherwise complete set: 20 secp256r1, 21 brainpoolP256r1, 23 secp192r1, 24 secp224r1, 25 brainpoolP384r1, 26 brainpoolP512r1, 27 secp521r1. Both verifiers instantiate verify_ecdsa with identical <97,48> parameters and both fields are 4-limb 384-bit, so the branch is 25 with the curve types swapped and no limb plumbing changed.

3_512_3_3_336_264_NA.provenance: RECOVERED by implementing verify_rsa's missing HASH_SIZE==64 block. It had been quarantined as fail-open: SIG_TYPE 3 dispatches to verify_rsa with this profile's HASH_ALGO=64, only the 32 and 20 blocks existed, and every pkcs assertion lives inside those blocks - so it computed sig^e mod n and asserted nothing.
3_512_3_3_336_264_NA.constants_derivation: Every constant in the new block was READ OFF a real EM rather than hand-assembled: EM = 00 01 || FF*170 || 00 || DigestInfo(19) || H(64) for k=256, split into 120-bit limbs least-significant first. The model is corroborated because it independently reproduces exp_result[16]==0x1ff.. and exp_result[17]==0x00, which the SHA-256 N=18 case already asserts for the same modulus size.

4_160_3_3_336_216_1_1296_3_256.provenance: Derived. SIG_TYPE 4 has no published Noir artifact; the tuple comes from rarimo circom RegisterIdentityBuilder, whose 10 template parameters ARE the profile name in order (SIGNATURE_TYPE, DG_HASH_TYPE, DOCUMENT_TYPE, EC_BLOCK_NUMBER, EC_SHIFT, DG1_SHIFT, AA_SIGNATURE_ALGO, DG15_SHIFT, DG15_BLOCK_NUMBER, AA_SHIFT). That decoding is validated against the 44 other named profiles: 8 of its 9 positional identities hold 44/44, and both block bounds (EC_LEN <= EC_BLOCK_NUMBER*blk, DG15_LEN <= DG15_BLOCK_NUMBER*blk) hold 44/44.
4_160_3_3_336_216_1_1296_3_256.provenance_dg15_len: DG15_LEN=165 is the DER length of a dg15 holding a 1024-bit RSA AA key with e=65537, counted byte by byte: 6F 81 A2 | 30 81 9F | AlgId 15 | 03 81 8D 00 | 30 81 89 | 02 81 81 00 | 128 | 02 03 01 00 01. INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED: the same derivation puts the modulus payload at byte 32, and AA_SHIFT=32 comes from the profile name separately - two unrelated routes agreeing on the same offset. It is also the modal live value (13 of 28 with AA_SIG_TYPE=1, AA_SHIFT=32); the 163s are the e=3 variant, which the same derivation predicts exactly.
4_160_3_3_336_216_1_1296_3_256.provenance_ec_len: EC_LEN=182 = DG15_SHIFT + DG_HASH_ALGO, i.e. the dg15 hash sits last in ec. Holds for 41 of 44 AA profiles, and is inside the block bound [182,192] forced by EC_BLOCK_NUMBER=3.
4_160_3_3_336_216_1_1296_3_256.superseded: An earlier derivation from circom signal counts gave DG15_LEN=138/EC_LEN=182, which is unsatisfiable: it fixes DG15_LEN+EC_LEN=320 while the read bounds force >=160 and >=182 (sum >=342). The signal-count input was the wrong one, not the bounds.

quarantined.name: ID_Card_I
quarantined.reason: NOT LOST - published upstream and byte-identical to our copy, but never migrated off UltraPlonk by ANYONE. rarimo still ships it as `BaseUltraVerifier` with vk.num_inputs = 5 and the same VK hash d5c1a3d188155b4a470c470501e5c729ec1dfa7a3fd839ee67a74eafb5b596a3. Under a bb 6.0-only app it cannot verify anything, and no 6.0 version exists in either repo.
quarantined.what_i_got_wrong: I claimed ID_Card_I WAS register_identity_light_td1 and marked it resolved. The evidence was that MY build of that circuit came out byte-identical to RegisterIdentityLightID256HonkVerifier - which proves those two are the same circuit, and says nothing about the legacy artifact. 5 != 3 refutes it outright, and the count was in my own notes before I drew the conclusion.
quarantined.still_correct: Deleting the duplicate I built WAS right: it really was a byte-identical copy of an already tested verifier, occupying a legacy slot. What was wrong is the inference that the slot was therefore covered.
quarantined.to_reopen: A 6.0 regeneration, which needs the circuit rarimo has not published, or its 14-generic tuple. Its 5 public signals match no circuit we have (register_identity and register_identity_td1 return 6, register_identity_light_td1 returns 3), so it predates the current output tuple.
quarantined.zk_type_casing_trap: ⚠️ THE LABEL IS UPPERCASE WHILE THE FILENAME IS MIXED CASE. rarimo defines Z_NOIR_PASSPORT_ID_CARD_I, not ..._ID_Card_I, so "Z_NOIR_PASSPORT_" + filename gives 0x5c30d28a591f489f7c7a5b7d18da1d596e1294076ec96f9b438fb3d3697d5951 - a key nothing would ever look up. The 88 numeric profiles have no letters, so the scheme is safe for them and ONLY for them. Anything non-numeric added later must take its label from rarimo scripts/utils/types.ts, not from the file name.
quarantined.what_is_it: A generic ID-card (TD1) registration circuit from the Noir/UltraPlonk era - NOT country specific. rarimo keeps country circuits in sibling directories (`geo`, `mne`); this one sits in the generic `noir` set. Its source circuit is in NEITHER noir circuits repo, which publish only register_identity, register_identity_light_td1 and the query circuits, so nothing here or upstream can regenerate it.
quarantined.status: WONT DO (owner, 2026-08-13) - closed, not blocked. Do not spend more time on it.
quarantined.why_closed: Its document class is already covered FIVE ways. TD1 coverage went from 1 profile to 5 this session (SIG_TYPE 1, 14, 21, 25 plus register_identity_td1), spanning RSA-PKCS, RSA-PSS, brainpoolP256, brainpoolP384 and secp192, with and without Active Authentication. ID_Card_I would add a sixth SOD LAYOUT, not a new capability, and no issuer in the ICAO PKD is known to need it - it is a layout identifier, not an algorithm, so it appears in no country DSC set.
quarantined.if_it_ever_matters: A real TD1 card failing to register with a layout none of the five match. The tuple falls out of that failing document; nothing else recovers it. Chasing it before that signal is speculation.
